name: Consensus-cluster aggregation vs median on the banked P278 template measurements — and a registered NEGATIVE for the block
registered_before_run: 2026-10-26 (frozen before any arithmetic on the template sets; the frozen input is the already-published out/p278/p278_raw.json, hash-pinned below)
honest_label: IN-SAMPLE RE-ANALYSIS. The rule was conceived after the 112 P278 template measurements were visible, so it cannot be a prospective test. Its job is to decide whether 'the object is a minority of the templates and the median throws it away' explains the data. The prospective test is P280 (fresh stereo pairs, frozen rule).
question: P278 showed that the true disparity is present among the templates on every row, but the median of all templates picked a background value on the thin board (rel 0.2963). Does a plurality/consensus rule — take the largest cluster of mutually consistent template disparities — recover the board, leave the controls alone, and (as predicted) still fail on the block whose bbox admits only three samples?

inputs.gt: the P277 recorded Z_gt per row, unchanged
inputs.no_new_computation: no model calls and no image matching: this experiment is arithmetic over the 112 banked template measurements

rule.R1_baseline: median of all valid template disparities (the P278 estimator), recomputed here for comparison
rule.R2_consensus: single-linkage clustering of the valid template disparities with a gap tolerance of 5 px; pick the cluster with the most members; ties broken by the higher mean NCC of the cluster, then by the lower median disparity; estimate = the median disparity of the chosen cluster
rule.R3_negative_control: one uniformly random valid template per row, seed 20261026
rule.R4_ncc_single: the single template with the highest NCC
rule.validity_clause: disparities < 0 are invalid (rectified stereo, positive baseline) and are dropped before aggregation; a row with fewer than two valid templates is non-evaluable, not a control

predictions.claim: FIX ON THE BOARD: under R2 the Lampshade1 yellow board reaches rel_err < 0.15 (P278's median gave 0.2963).
predictions.falsifies: Board stays >= 0.15: the minority-object explanation is wrong even with a single-linkage plurality rule.

predictions.claim: NO REGRESSION: all 11 evaluable controls keep rel_err < 0.15 under R2 and shift by <= 0.05 of GT relative to R1.
predictions.falsifies: Any evaluable control loses its pass or shifts >5%: the plurality rule is not safe as a default.

predictions.claim: REGISTERED NEGATIVE: the Monopoly block is NOT fixed under R2 (rel_err >= 0.15), because its bbox admits only three templates and, after the validity clause, the two survivors are singletons — the tie-break goes to the higher-NCC sample (421 px, NCC 0.617 vs 0.571). This prediction CONFIRMS the diagnosis 'three samples are structurally insufficient', it is not a failure.
predictions.falsifies: If the block IS fixed under R2, the 'sample count' diagnosis is wrong and the block's recovery must have another explanation.

predictions.claim: NEGATIVE CONTROL: R3 (random template) fails at least 3 of the 11 evaluable controls, i.e. the rule is not trivially 'any pick works'.
predictions.falsifies: Random picking passes 9+ controls: then the control cohort is too easy to discriminate rules and the comparison is uninformative.

predictions.claim: MECHANISM ON THE BOARD: the winning cluster has >= 3 members and its median lies within 15% of the true disparity, while the median of all templates does not — the object's templates form a plurality but not a majority.
predictions.falsifies: Winning cluster has <3 members or its median is >15% from truth: the 'minority but plurality' story does not describe what happened.

gate.hash_gate: if the sha256 of out/p278/p278_raw.json does not equal the frozen value, the run is INCONCLUSIVE and no prediction is scored (same no-partial-credit rule as P278)
